action: Sites using Optimizely Web Experimentation: confirm your snippet is clean, review what loaded for visitors since November 16, and assess whether payment data was exposed. Visitors who paid on affected sites should watch card statements.
attack: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
exec: One compromised web supplier put harmful code on 178 organisations' sites, creating customer fraud risk and possible breach duties.
plain: Attackers tampered with a website tool from Optimizely, so 178 organisations' websites, including major news and retail sites, loaded harmful code. It could reportedly steal card details. Optimizely says the code is removed.

key_findings: Optimizely says an unauthorised party exploited a flaw in the Web Experimentation account signup flow to impersonate users and insert malicious JavaScript into customer projects.
It detected the activity on November 16 and says it closed the flaw within three hours of detection.
On November 17 it reported the code removed and affected accounts secured; on November 18 it said remediation was complete and every Web Experimentation customer had been contacted.
Optimizely says less than 5% of its customers were impacted and that it was not a credentials breach.
The 178-organisation count and the script behaviour come from researchers and news coverage, not Optimizely.

Zscaler ThreatLabz (Nov 18) reports more than 450 unique domains and more than 3,000 URLs serving the malicious script across 12 industries, a wider count than the 178 organisations; it names no actor.
recommendations: Customers using Web Experimentation should review the additional guidance Optimizely sent them and contact Optimizely Support with questions.

sources.name: Optimizely status: Web Experimentation Security Incident

summary: Optimizely says an unauthorised party exploited a flaw in its Web Experimentation signup flow to inject malicious JavaScript into some customer projects. It reports the flaw fixed and code removed, and on November 18 said under 5% of customers were affected. Researcher Scott Helme counted 178 organisations; coverage says the code skimmed cards and swapped crypto addresses. Krebs, citing Report URI, says about $7,500 was stolen.
title: Optimizely script injection reaches 178 organizations' websites

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Optimizely report. The 178-organisation count and the script's behaviour come from a researcher and news coverage, not Optimizely. Krebs on Security and Sophos X-Ops read in the 2026-11-19 sweep; Krebs figures (26 rebuilds, about $7,500, iOS exploit kits) are attributed to Report URI. Status page re-read 2026-11-19: Nov 18 update says remediation complete and under 5% of customers affected. Zscaler ThreatLabz blog read 2026-11-19: more than 450 domains and 3,000 URLs, no attribution.
